summary: Uptime watches your websites and APIs on a schedule and tells you only when a failure is confirmed. It never calls a missing check healthy, and it keeps the evidence behind every incident. Alerts go to email, Slack or a signed webhook.
does: Check web pages and API responses for the right status, text, headers, data values and speed
Check that a server port answers, that DNS records are right, and that SSL certificates and domain registrations are not about to expire
Choose how many failed checks in a row open an incident and how many passes close it
Show a time as Unknown when no check arrived, instead of guessing it was fine
Watch cron jobs and nightly backups through heartbeat check-ins
Alert you by email, Slack or a signed webhook, and run an alert drill to learn whether a message really reaches someone
Pause alerts during planned maintenance windows
Run checks from a machine on your own network and export your monitors, evidence and alert history any time

promises.text: One failed check never raises an alarm. A monitor is called Failing only after confirmation, a missing check shows as Unknown, and it recovers only on fresh passing checks.
Every scheduled check and every retry is kept with its time, result and error type, and a retry never erases an earlier failure.
Only confirmed incident changes send automatic alerts, and a test send never changes a monitor's status.
Each alert gets one automatic send per destination where a repeat could double up, an unclear outcome is not sent again, and 'accepted' is never reported as 'read'.
An alert drill sends a clearly marked test with a one-time confirmation link, and a confirmation is the recipient's own report, never proof of monitoring.
Certificate checks look at trust, host name and expiry from each location, warn in stages before a certificate runs out, and clear only after a new valid certificate is seen.
Planned and recurring maintenance windows use US time zones and daylight saving, and keep the underlying check results so reports still show what happened.
A backup restores only into an empty installation: monitors come back paused, destinations disabled and old alerts held back.
Every address and redirect is validated, unsafe addresses are refused, and a redirect that downgrades from HTTPS is rejected.
An owner can erase a monitor with its evidence, an alert destination, or an operator, and gets a receipt of what was removed.

summary: Orbit puts a deal in your NOW queue when a customer replies, scores it from real signals, and shows you why. Your company's policy controls agent sending; with approval required, a person reviews the exact email before it is sent. It is free for the whole team, and you can try it beside your current CRM.
does: Move a deal into your NOW queue when a customer replies, books a meeting or submits a form
Score each deal from what customers actually did, with older activity counting for less and every signal behind the score shown
Keep contacts, companies and deals, with your own fields, in a pipeline with your own stages
Let a contact form on your site drop each enquiry onto the right contact
Draft follow-ups, with optional AI, that you review and approve one by one, and schedule them with quiet hours
Cancel scheduled follow-ups automatically when the customer replies
Pull in emails and meetings from Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, forwarded mail or a calendar link
Import contacts from a CSV, and export or restore a complete archive of your workspace any time

promises.text: Signals, scores and AI text never grant permission to send. Your company's policy decides agent sending; when approval is required, a person approves the exact saved recipients, subject and body, and later changes invalidate it.
A deal's score shows every signal it used, with source, time and weight, beside the reason for the recommendation.
Orbit uses no tracking script, pixel or cookie, and does not fingerprint visitors.
A reply, a booked meeting, an unsubscribe or a permanent bounce cancels that contact's scheduled messages.

Opt-out is on by default for sequence email and off for one-to-one email. Messages set to carry it include one-click unsubscribe; an identified opt-out marks the contact do-not-contact within a minute and cancels scheduled messages.
A draft goes stale when the customer replies or the deal changes, and a stale draft cannot be sent until you have seen what changed.
Capture never writes a draft or sends a message, and a contact created from captured mail is do-not-contact until you clear it.
If the AI is unavailable, records, scoring, search, hand-written drafts and sending still work.
Merging duplicates needs you to choose the surviving record and every conflicting value, and refuses if either record changed after your review.
Deleting a contact removes their email, signals, drafts and message bodies from records, search, exports and later AI or mail requests within five minutes.

summary: Oncall shows everyone who is on call now, who is next and exactly when they hand over. It keeps rotations, swaps, incidents, runbooks and follow-ups in one place, and runs alongside the pager you already use while you move your schedules over.
does: Show who is on call now, who is next and when the next hand-over happens
Build primary and backup rotations in your team's timezone, so a hand-over stays on the same clock time when clocks change
Cover a few hours with an override or swap without touching the rotation
Subscribe to a private calendar feed of the next seven days of shifts
Record alerts from monitoring, route them to the right service and replay the routing safely
Declare an incident, assign a commander, follow the runbook and keep every decision on a timeline
Resolve with recovery evidence and a summary, then track follow-up tasks and review
Preview your Opsgenie or PagerDuty schedules before anything is imported

promises.text: Oncall sends no texts, calls or push alerts, so your existing pager stays in charge while you use it.
Oncall sends signed response events only to endpoints an administrator approves; paging stays off, and email is for sign-in links only.
A runbook is copied into the incident when it is declared, so later edits never rewrite instructions mid-incident.
Resolving an incident needs recovery evidence and a summary, and every change is recorded in an attributed timeline.
Incident records you write are never deleted automatically.
Rotations hand over by wall-clock time in your named zone, and clock-change gaps show up as visible gaps.
Viewers can only read, responders coordinate, and admins manage; alert-sending credentials grant no read access, and removed access stops on the next request.
Replaying alert routing only reads: it creates no alert, incident or outside effect.
A move-in preview writes nothing, a person must review it before it is applied, and imported schedules stay paused.
A move-in can be undone, and edits you made afterwards are kept rather than overwritten.
